correctness.rationale: The full autocorrelation proof is reconstructed for all positive magnitudes; highest coefficient fixes d, second yields two-circle geometry, first yields an explicit quadratic/antilinear identity. For nonzero second correlation, two-circle equality is equivalent to the strict triangle. At zero second correlation, a cubic gives the universal three cap and root-of-unity equality classification. Converse choices of phases are constructive. The independent packaged checker passes exact arithmetic witness and over 300 numerical tests, supplemental to the proof.

value.rationale: A complete sharp identifiability criterion for an experimentally natural fixed-amplitude Pauli problem on the smallest support permitting nontrivial ambiguities. The strict triangle divides the full four-dimensional positive magnitude cone into uniquely identifiable and ambiguous domains; the maximal-fiber criterion determines exact boundary geometry. This goes beyond previously reported isolated counterexamples.
